messages:
Maria: quick summary — ran an nsys capture on the canary that hit the 2x tail-latency regression. results point to a burst of KV write kernels during long contexts when prefetch is enabled.
Maria: nsys command I used: ```nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn -o /tmp/run1 nvidia_launcher ./redwood_infer --model xlarge --profile-prefix kv_prefetch```
Devon: can you drop the top timeline flame or a screenshot?
Maria: pasted the timeline snippet below (trimmed):
```
GPU timeline: 00:00 - 00:12  fused_attn_v3  kernel  (high occupancy)
            00:03 - 00:06  kv_write_part   (spiky)
            00:06 - 00:09  kv_read_part    (steady)
            00:09 - 00:11  fallback_attn   (smaller grid, more copies)
```
Maria: notice the kv_write_part spikes align with small batch tail latencies.
Riley: this smells like the batching heuristics were changed in last roll — we moved to earlier flush for partial batches which could cause more frequent KV flushes.
Riley: small batches -> repeated KV writes rather than amortizing across a big batch.
Zhen: another angle: kernel selection fallback logic sometimes picks the legacy kernel for sequences > 4096 on that model variant because of tile-size heuristics. legacy kernel writes KV out-of-place.
Devon: any nvprof runs to compare kernel durations?
Maria: ran nvprof on a reduced repro. nvprof shows kv_write_part 3.2ms -> 10.1ms with prefetch on; fused_attn_v3 increases latency by ~7%.
Kevin: uploaded a perfetto trace to the perf bucket: gs://redwood-perf/traces/2062003333-perfetto.pb (private link)
Kevin: perfetto shows PCIe memcpy bursts coincident with writes — so host-device copy activity is up.
perf-bot: Automated job 2062003333-nsys-diff completed. diff summary: +2.8ms mean kv_write, +18% write calls, +11% GPU active time.
Zhen: +18% write calls matches the heuristic change theory. does the runtime still prefetch KV to device or is it writing back frequently?
Maria: runtime prefetch config: `PREFETCH_STRATEGY=aggressive`, `KV_WRITE_BACK=lazy` — but we saw explicit writeback calls at sequence end.
Riley: maybe the partial-flush triggered an eager writeback because we treat partial batches as boundaries. code: ```if (batch.partial) kv_manager.flush_writes(batch.id)```
Riley: that `flush_writes` was introduced in the batching PR to reduce memory pressure. it might be too aggressive.
Devon: quick experiments: 1) disable prefetch; 2) revert partial flush conditional to only flush if mem>threshold; 3) force fused_attn_v3 for long sequences (bypass tile heuristic). which one should I run first?
Maria: start with disabling prefetch (env `PREFETCH_STRATEGY=none`) — cheapest & fastest. if that reduces write calls, it's a prefetch interaction.
Kevin: I can run an A/B on the canary cluster and capture nsys. I'll schedule slot in 30m.
Maria: also please run with `NVTX` markers around KV ops so we can correlate in perfetto.
Zhen: if disabling prefetch helps, we should explore modifying `flush_writes` to be size-aware and add an option `kv_write_coalesce_window_ms` to batch small writebacks.
Devon: agree. also check kernel selection path: add a debug toggle to force fused_attn_v3 for the sample and see if that changes copies.
Riley: small note — the batcher recently started emitting `flush_writes` for any partial that has >1 token consumed to avoid OOM under concurrency. that threshold can be bumped.
Maria: follow-ups: Kevin will run A/B traces with prefetch=none vs prefetch=aggressive; Devon will add NVTX markers and a forced-kernel toggle; Zhen will prototype coalescing window; Riley will revert/bump partial flush threshold in a local build.
Kevin: starting run now — will post nsys link when done.
perf-bot: nsys upload complete: gs://redwood-perf/results/2062003333-nsys.html
Maria: thanks. once we have both traces, let's meet briefly to decide rollout plan. my current hypothesis: batching heuristic + aggressive prefetch => frequent small KV writebacks => PCIe memcpy spikes => fused/kernel fallback copy overhead => tail latency regression.
Devon: sounds plausible. also check pinned vs pageable memory allocations for KV buffers — pageable can add host-side copies.
Zhen: good catch. I'll look at allocator metrics next.
Maria: great. short sync in 1hr after results. :thumbsup:
